sustaining.method: Allocate the linked FY2027 consolidated sustaining cash anchor using an equal-weighted blend of normalized FY2025 continuing and 9M2026 consolidated accrual shares. Exclude divested sites from the FY2025 denominator. Retain the corporate line separately. Scale sustaining capital with modeled site activity measured at FY2027 unit CAS. Annual escalation in this packet is real and separate from nominal NAV inflation. The FY2026 attributable site guide supplies a reasonableness comparison and differs in scope from consolidated accrual capital.

cadia_panel_caves.budget_basis: Combined Newmont post-acquisition development estimates for PC2-3 and PC1-2. Newcrest's prior expenditures are sunk. The Q4 allocation uses the initial site target less reported 9M project development as an analyst bridge.
cadia_panel_caves.method: Subtract the September cumulative cost and the Q4 bridge from the post-acquisition budget midpoint. Allocate the remainder 50%, 30% and 20% in 2027, 2028 and 2029 following PC2-3 handover and through the planned last PC1-2 drawbell. The annual weights are analyst assumptions.

lihir_nearshore_barrier.budget_basis: Fully funded in February 2026. Budget is the full project cost and the September cumulative amount excludes capitalized interest and D&A.
lihir_nearshore_barrier.method: Use the initial $140 million 2026 target and the indicated 2027 ramp. The analyst assigns $100 million of the portfolio's indicated 2027 development increase to Lihir and assigns the budget midpoint remainder to the disclosed 2028 completion year.

cerro_negro_district_expansion_1.budget_basis: Issuer budget for District Expansion 1. The latest interim filing describes the cumulative spend line as the Cerro Negro expansion projects. The bridge uses it as a budget-spend proxy.
cerro_negro_district_expansion_1.method: Allocate the remaining midpoint budget equally over 2027–2029. Completion year and equal annual payments are analyst assumptions. No separate incremental resource ounces are added to the proved and probable reserve case.

tanami_expansion_2.budget_basis: Company projects $1,700–$1,800 million and targets commercial production toward the end of H1 2027 in its October update.
tanami_expansion_2.method: Use the February presentation's $335 million 2026 project spending reference and the October interim filing's $192 million actual to approximate Q4. The balance of the midpoint falls in FY2027, already inside the near-term forecast.

ngm_goldrush.budget_basis: Barrick discloses gross project economics. This row uses Newmont's 38.5% proportionately consolidated share of the operator's $1 billion target and $531 million cumulative spend.
ngm_goldrush.method: Use the $14 million 100% Q3 project cost to approximate Q4 and an analyst $300 million 100% project allocation for FY2027 given infrastructure work. Put the remaining $155 million gross in FY2028, when Barrick expects full production. The Newmont-share 2027 allocation is already embedded in near-term capital.

ngm_ren.budget_basis: Barrick's $410–$470 million estimate and $246 million cumulative spend are on a 100% basis. This row uses Newmont's 38.5% share.
ngm_ren.method: Use the $28 million 100% Q3 project cost as a Q4 proxy and place the remaining midpoint balance in FY2027, when Barrick expects full production. Newmont's combined FY2027 Goldrush and Ren modeled capital of $179.41 million fits within its $240 million initial FY2026 NGM development capital reference.

red_chris_block_cave_option.method: British Columbia amended the environmental certificate and issued permit amendments after Tahltan consent. Feasibility, final JV and corporate approval, and federal grant terms remained pending at the cutoff. Real project costs include contingency, are stated on a 100% basis after the proposed grant and exclude open-pit-to-block-cave transition costs. No block cave production, costs, or grant proceeds enter base mine cash after the conditional increment is removed. The June 2025 permit application expected the last open-pit ore in 2027 and stockpile processing through 2028 under its economic assumptions. Pit extension was under review. The FY2025 reserve footnotes explicitly include underground gold and copper, so combined site reserves cannot support a longer open-pit horizon.

development.method: Project cash in 2028 and 2029 is incremental to sustaining capex. Q4 2026 and 2027 approved project spending stays in the linked forecast. Allocate the unsplit 2027 group increase of $500 million as $100 million to approved Lihir and $400 million to conditional Red Chris. Apply the linked 2216/2211 consolidated cash conversion to the conditional amount. Retain the FY2026 preapproval site spending reference within the remaining 2027 portfolio envelope. The split and later-year schedule are analyst assumptions. No recurring unspecified growth capital or incremental resource conversion is assumed after the explicit projects.

closure.method: Start with FY2025 undiscounted contractual obligations. Deduct 9M2026 cash and the Q4 2026, 2027 and 2028 management-based cash outlook once. Use the September 2026 total book provision as the calibration target for future explicit payments plus the residual. The 4.2% rate is an analyst proxy based on annualized 9M accretion to opening book value, cross-checked to FY2025. Newmont uses credit-adjusted risk-free rates and a market risk premium. Calculate one effective maturity for the remaining nominal cash and allocate it across adjacent calendar year-ends to preserve present value at the calibration rate. Actual settlement may span decades. The residual incorporates no separate estimate of changes in nominal obligations since FY2025. All closure cash is deducted once at the group level, with no additional deduction of the opening book provision. No comparable Merian cash schedule was identified to credit noncontrolling interests for their economic share.
